newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Proposed Israeli law to bar intifada damage claims.
newsitem.headline: Proposed Israeli law to bar intifada damage claims.

text.p: Lulu Abu Daheh was six when a stray bullet fired by an Israeli soldier during the Palestinian national uprising smashed into her head, her parents say.
Eight years later, they cannot afford to buy their paralysed daughter the special wheelchair she needs. They were forced to take her out of a hospice when funds ran dry.

Abu Daheh's family has sued in an Israeli court for damages but a proposed law that would bar most Palestinians from seeking compensation for injuries incurred in the uprising that ended in 1993 with an interim Israel-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace deal may foil their suit.
The bill came up in Israel's parliament on Monday. A vote was delayed until Tuesday but analysts expected it would pass its first reading. To become law it must pass three readings.
"We need more money," said Kamilia Abu Daheh, carrying her daughter in her arms after spending the day pleading with Israeli parliament members to defeat the bill.
The legislation classifies the intifada as a war, in which case Israel would not be liable for damages.
Palestinians who can prove that Israeli soldiers intentionally hurt them could still receive compensation.
"We find it abominable," said Uri Avneri, an Israeli peace activist. "It is a law against people who have been killed, maimed or wounded in the intifada -- not participants, but innocent bystanders."
About 30 peace activists protested outside parliament on Monday. Signs they held read: "Robbing the victims."
"When damage is inflicted on purpose, then one can claim compensatory damages," said Israel government spokesman Moshe Fogel.
He said the intifada should be treated as a war because soldiers faced a "belligerent population" and "terror squads".
The uprising began in December 1987. It was aimed at ending Israel's occupation of the West Bank and Gaza Strip, areas the Jewish state captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
Israelis killed 1,206 Palestinians during the intifada, which subsided with the signing of the 1993 Israel-PLO interim peace deal. Palestinians killed 179 Israelis.
Palestinians have filed 4,000 claims for damages totalling tens of millions of dollars, Israel's Justice Ministry said.
Fogel said Israel felt it had acted with restraint during the intifada.
"Our forces used rubber bullets and tear gas in a manner that saved Palestinian lives," he said.
"We do not believe that when coming to deal with payment of damages that the hostile activities directed at us should be seen as a civilian situation," he said.
